evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses adjacency bitmasks and degree ordering; deepseek explicitly comments "Try to find an independent set of size k"
affordance_in_statement: Whenever a member is added to the panel, every other member who shares an interaction event with them is flagged as incompatible. A member cannot be added to the panel if they have been flagged as incompatible by any member already on the panel.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving rewording that removes this equivalence: a valid panel is intrinsically an independent set of size k in the interaction graph. Only changing the selection rules or the underlying task would eliminate it.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the process is exactly finding an independent set and solves it with bitmask branch-and-bound.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The incompatibility rules make every pair of selected members nonadjacent in the interaction graph.

common_affordance: The panel-selection process is equivalent to finding an independent set of size k in the undirected interaction graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It recognized the independent-set formulation but used straightforward recursive backtracking, which is vulnerable to exponential blowup at n=46.

It attempted to enumerate size-k subsets using a meet-in-the-middle approach, which is not sufficiently controlled for the full n=46 search space and may also incur excessive reconstruction/enumeration cost.
Its core routine is named and structured as find_clique, solving the opposite adjacency condition rather than selecting pairwise non-interacting members.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can defeat the surviving approach: the independent-set structure is the core task. Defeating it would require changing the selection semantics, such as making incompatibility directional or time-dependent, which changes the problem.
